item.text: {"code":"","conclusion":"Primary result: The recorded analysis of 8,773 respondents reports a weak positive SES–BA completion correlation (point-biserial r=0.061233; claim cd531cb148206025ceb1a010a6a02d6c5d7c42343a9a987022811b9fbe36d77f; evidence 36a8a70816bb64d1c35efd4bf65b3a7d574b83e3138decaf0a47bfeae501913d). Overall, 236 respondents completed a BA (2.690072%). Completion was 0.683761% in the bottom SES quintile and 3.532764% in the top quintile (1,755 respondents each), a 2.849003 percentage-point gap using empirical thresholds with boundary ties retained (gap claim 002a2d8b3122c915df6b5e16b64e8c493de661eecb56991d0ef4bf412d9e93a4; evidence 417b41a31d00128afa27898fa7e7e0e491f1bb6b70bdbb53dca163e7c2a6e5c5; rates also recorded in evidence 1cd71aeba536613a35635ec34a175d64fe2ea8938ee4d774d71cf22dba88a4d8). An unadjusted logistic model reports 42.1% higher odds per one sample SD higher SES: OR=1.420623 (claim ca6b265d589cc4896226b29dada2be05f421f0fbcc63daacb522f1535877b31f; evidence 31098b21b23c2c5977fdce18e59e8b31904eb9faf3297c3052f6a184681b32cc), with HC0 robust Wald 95% CI [1.269144, 1.590182] under independent observations (claim d533d9b4dde05c526faa99adfc10379ebada7524421dd243a285128d7029c253; evidence e38d43214ba1fddc5f0e71d2853a12fb66c3127c7b7cb3fab693def1139509d9). Thus the reported association is small in correlation and absolute percentage-point terms, but appreciable relative to the low completion prevalence.\n\nQualification result: The planned five-bin SES sensitivity check returned no facts because it could not locate exactly one nls_ses_processed.csv under /input/data. Its recorded execution status was succeeded, but the substantive check was not completed; it provides no evidence of robustness or monotonicity (execution-only claim faa2082fe658cdc05ff7b8abb8b7e8ff18953c15ea53889b287cd008c41b6dd5; evidence 359938f30b6f1d7707bdbc1bf38113036c9705a65011c546c53fca7917429610).","limitations":["The profile reports no missing values, and the primary analysis excluded zero rows for missing/invalid SES or outcome. Boolean true/false was mapped to completion/noncompletion consistently with the supplied outcome description; no outcome/indicator mismatch is apparent.","These are unadjusted observational associations, not causal effects; demographic and academic confounding and selection remain possible.","No survey weights or sampling-design information were supplied. Results describe analyzed respondents; the confidence interval assumes independent observations.","The logistic model assumes linear SES effects on log odds. Its odds ratio is not a risk ratio. SES units are undocumented.","Quintile boundaries retain ties. The uncompleted sensitivity check proposed a strictly greater-than upper threshold, unlike the primary inclusive threshold, so its intended top group was not identical.","Ledger support verifies recorded output and execution/input binding only, not statistical correctness or scientific validity. No independent scientific validation or successful functional-form sensitivity result is available."]}
